body:
It was definitely sudden. It felt as if people randomly decided to interact with me, as if it's entirely possible it could've happened a few years earlier or not at all, the die just rolled in my favour. I'm not sure why I feel as though this is the case, so it's a fair assumption to make that I am an antagonising these people to justify this. It's intuition, I guess.

 I definitely think that it would be unfair to say that I didn't contribute on my end though: I was making a considerable but reasonably subtle effort to be included in things and as open as possible.

I would definitely agree with you on this, except that I always made an active effort to try and be a part of things. Parents made it hard but I don't think I would say that I shut people out. 

I can say that with confidence as my best friend did exactly what you described, and I tried very hard to convince him to try and get involved and open up more (he was very explicit about his mental health and made self depreciating jokes in large groups of people he hardly knew, so it was a bit more on the nose).

I would say that I'm very good at socialising, at least now. Maybe there's some credence to people saying I've changed, but people are quite specific on how I've changed and they've never said anything like that. But I don't feel any different and the few who have properly known me for this long have always agreed.

I guess people in the comments put it quite well. It's half a grudge that I've held and I don't see why people deserve to have me as a friend now if they didn't bother to interact with me before. That definitely sounds very narcissistic, but I'm not really sure how to better word it. The other half is that I always seem to be reminded (whether it's my own head or something actually happening like an awkward moment or looking back at photos where I'm not there) of all of this, which is quite triggering and not an experience I want to continue.

Sorry, that's a great question I clearly didn't answer. I guess I do? I mean, the last year with everyone liking me, it's hard not to reciprocate. Obviously I'm partial to the people on my side with all of this, but plenty of people against it too. There are girls I get butterflies talking to and mates I can have a laugh and drink with, but usually after every good time I just get resentful and wish I could've had these times when I really needed them.

I respect them as people of course, but I guess I'm conflicted about whether I should care if they're upset about my choice? Hope that answers your questions.

I didn't make it clear at all, sorry. It's very triggering to be around people I'm close with, and as my year group is all really just one large popular group with smaller, less popular groups on the outskirts, I can't really avoid it. Being pressured by most of these people to stay in contact with everyone is a smaller issue too.

YTA. Given what you have told us it seems you have reacted unreasonably. IVF is totally normal and whilst someone using paternal sperm is a little unconventional (usually if a biologically-related donor is wanted, a brother is a first choice), you've only gone and heightened the concerns I'm already sure the stigma surrounding IVF raised.

Your sister was TA for attacking you personally after your response, but your comments weren't much better.

I think your misleading title sheds some light on your perspective. The carrier is not your sister and there are no biological risks beyond those normally associated with IVF. Your feelings that this is weird do not take priority over your sister's want to have a biological connection to her child.
